boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Taylor University traditions spanning performances, races, cultural celebration, residence-hall events, and basketball.

cards.title: Silent Night
cards.subtitle: Taylor men’s basketball tradition
cards.notes: Attend the final men’s basketball game before Christmas break; remain silent until Taylor scores its tenth point, then join the celebration and closing song.
cards.short_summary: A costumed crowd holds its cheers for the Trojans’ tenth point.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor identifies Silent Night as its biggest basketball game of the year, with students silent until Taylor’s tenth point and a student-led rendition of “Silent Night” at the end.
cards.access_notes: The official tradition page describes the event but does not state admission or access requirements.

cards.title: Taylathon
cards.subtitle: Inter-class bicycle relay race
cards.notes: Watch or support the class teams as riders exchange bicycles in the relay; the documented challenge is keeping transitions smooth so the bike never stops.
cards.short_summary: Graduating classes compete in a bicycle-passing relay.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor says Taylathon began in 1948 and pits the four graduating classes against one another in separate men’s and women’s bike relay races.
cards.access_notes: The official tradition page does not state spectator access or costs.

cards.title: Airband
cards.subtitle: Residence-hall lip-sync and choreography competition
cards.notes: See residence-hall acts perform planned group choreography to a song or mix of songs, then watch the judges name a winner.
cards.short_summary: Residence halls turn lip-syncing into a spring-stage competition.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor describes Airband as a spring lip-syncing and choreography competition between residence halls, judged after each group performs.
cards.access_notes: The official tradition page does not state admission or participation requirements.

cards.title: Envision Film Festival
cards.subtitle: Film-focused weekend at Taylor
cards.notes: Look for the festival’s public student-film screenings and talks by film professionals covering different parts of the filmmaking process.
cards.short_summary: A weekend combining film-industry talks with public student-film screenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor describes Envision Film Festival as a weekend with film professionals speaking about filmmaking and student films screened for the public.
cards.access_notes: The official page says student films are screened for the public but does not list ticketing details.

cards.title: Mosaic Night
cards.subtitle: Office of Intercultural Programs annual celebration
cards.notes: Experience performances, poetry, food, and cultural celebration presented by the Multi-Ethnic Student Association and Taylor’s intercultural community.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration of the cultures represented at Taylor.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor says Mosaic Night is the Office of Intercultural Programs’ annual celebration of 30+ countries and cultures, hosted by the Multi-Ethnic Student Association.
cards.access_notes: The official page describes registration for interested high-school attendees but does not state costs or current event details.

cards.title: Melon and Gourd
cards.subtitle: Third West Wengatz hall tradition
cards.notes: Observe this Third West Wengatz tag tradition from a respectful distance; participants carry a melon and gourd and use themed stunts to reach Friday Chapel.
cards.short_summary: A residence-hall tag game built around a melon, gourd, and chapel deadline.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor identifies Melon and Gourd as a Third West Wengatz tradition in which students carry a melon and gourd while trying not to be tagged.
cards.access_notes: This is a residence-hall tradition; do not enter residence areas unless invited and authorized.

cards.title: Nostalgia Night
cards.subtitle: Live student music from before the class’s birth year
cards.notes: Attend the live student music show featuring songs from before the graduating class was born; unlike Airband, the performances use real instruments.
cards.short_summary: Students perform older music live, without Airband-style lip-syncing.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor states that Nostalgia Night features students using real instruments to perform musical acts from before the graduating class was born.
cards.access_notes: The official tradition page does not state admission or schedule details.

cards.title: MyGen
cards.subtitle: Live student music from after the senior class’s birth year
cards.notes: Look for the companion show to Nostalgia Night, where students use real instruments to perform music released after the senior class was born.
cards.short_summary: A live-instrument student show focused on newer music.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor describes MyGen as a tradition in which students use real instruments to showcase music from after the senior class was born.
cards.access_notes: The official tradition page does not state admission or schedule details.

cards.title: Open Houses
cards.subtitle: Themed residence-wing and floor events
cards.notes: Visit only open, invited wings or floors to take part in their interactive theme; Taylor examples include Oregon Trail, Christmas, and Great Future Dads of America.
cards.short_summary: Residence halls welcome campus visitors into interactive themed spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor says students invite the campus to their wings or floors for interactive themed open houses and gives several residence-hall examples.
cards.access_notes: Enter only during an advertised open house and follow residence-hall access rules.

cards.title: Pick-a-Dates
cards.subtitle: Residence-floor and wing group outings
cards.notes: Join a casual group outing only if invited by the organizing floor or wing; the documented activities include bowling, canoeing, and roller-skating.
cards.short_summary: Floors and wings organize low-pressure group dates and outings.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor describes Pick-a-Dates as casual group dates organized by floors and wings, with activities such as bowling, canoeing, and roller-skating.
cards.access_notes: Participation depends on the organizing floor or wing; individual outings may have costs.
